notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Green wooded hills and tall golden grass; Lesotho's mountains are barren by contrast.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Dark brown wooden poles of simple design, insulators mostly on the side; three-insulator tops are more common here than elsewhere in the region.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Roads numbered MR are nearly exclusive to this country.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Yellow edge lines and occasionally triple white centre lines; shared with its neighbours.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: All coverage uses a white car with no antenna, as in South Africa, Lesotho and Botswana.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Long plates with green at the bottom; some South African plates look similar.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: Concrete bus shelters are common beside roads.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Western highlands have pristine golden montane grass and mountains.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Pine plantations in select areas of the west; similar ones occur across the border.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The central south, mainly along the MR9, is overwhelmingly dark green with tall wooded mountains.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The east is unusually flat with mountains often visible far away; sugar cane grows in several spots along the eastern border.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: The MR3 from Manzini to the border is the only divided highway, split by metal and stone guardrails.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: A savannah reserve with narrow dirt tracks and tall grass.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Text in the language of Mozambique suggests the small border town of Lomahasha.
